heading: Why We Invested in Wonderland
content:
# Why Now and Why This Team

## 1. Consumer Centricity Combined with High Quality Sourcing and Processing

With decades of experience in sourcing high-quality nuts and dry fruits globally, Wonderland's deep procurement expertise ensures they are able to offer customers high quality products. Further with the processing, and packaging functions being fully in-house, Wonderland ensures they retain agility in being able to respond to the evolving consumer preferences.

## 2. Strong Growth and Robust Profitability

We were impressed by the Wonderland team's ability to deliver exceptional growth and consistent profitability, demonstrating their disciplined mindset. This DNA is deeply embedded in all functions of the company with all efforts directed to making sure the customers are offered the best prices possible while maintaining healthy margins.

## 3. Market Tailwinds Towards Healthy Snacking

Rising health awareness, expanding quick-commerce channels, and the shift from unorganised to branded formats are accelerating category growth, positioning Wonderland to capture this momentum.

##  Empowering Communities, Driving Purpose

Their processing facilities employ nearly 1,000 workers in its production facilities, most of whom are women, providing equitable job opportunities, good working conditions and supporting economic empowerment.

The company is setting up a new integrated processing facility in Uttar Pradesh, which will be green-certified as per IGBC standards while anchoring local job creation. Wonderland's alignment with the 2X Challenge further underscores the commitment to empowering women through formal employment and skill development.

## Our Partnership Vision

For us, Wonderland represents far more than an investment but it's a long-term partnership to build India's most trusted and purposeful brand in the snacking space.

This investment, our largest to date at INR 140 crore, marks a strong conviction in both the founders' vision and the category's long-term potential. We're proud to lead this round alongside British International Investment (BII) and to back Rakesh and Anubhav as they scale their mission to make healthy snacking accessible, sustainable, and deeply rooted in trust.

At Asha Ventures, we believe that the future of consumer brands lies in mindful consumption and inclusive growth and Wonderland Foods is an exemplary embodiment of that belief. We're excited to stand alongside them in this journey building a brand that not only fuels the nation's appetite but also nourishes its people and communities.

heading: Why We Invested in Automony
content:
# India's Commercial Vehicle Backbone - A Quiet Giant

India's logistics economy runs on wheels and at its core lies the commercial vehicle (CV) sector. But what many overlook is the sheer dominance of used commercial vehicles in powering this backbone. Over 55-60% of all commercial vehicles sold in India are used vehicles, not new ones. The Indian used CV market is already 2x the size of the new CV market in terms of transaction volumes.

Nearly 80% of India's 6+ million small fleet operators and owner-drivers rely on used vehicles due to affordability. The opportunity is especially concentrated in Tier 2 and Tier 3 India, which accounts for ~70% of national CV movement, driven by local logistics, intra-city supply chains, agriculture mobility, and construction demand. This is a massive market but one with deep structural gaps.

## The Credit Problem: A Roadblock to Livelihoods

For small operators, truck owners, and micro-enterprises across Tier 2 and 3 India, a used commercial vehicle is their bread and butter yet access to credit remains their biggest barrier. Many are pushed toward informal lenders who charge extremely high interest rates, eroding their already thin margins. Traditional financiers avoid the segment due to high fragmentation, asset variability, lack of formal documentation, and perceived risk. As a result, financing penetration for used commercial vehicles is less than 25%, far below other retail lending segments.

This gap keeps millions of hardworking operators from upgrading their vehicles, expanding their routes, or improving their earnings trapping them in low-income cycles.

## A Market Ripe for Innovation

Despite the market size and critical role used CVs play, very few institutional players were building for this segment. The ecosystem lacked organised distribution channels outside large metros and data-led risk assessment tailored to small fleet operators.

It was a classic case of a large, underserved, complex market one that needed a team with deep domain expertise, disciplined execution, and a strong mission orientation. 

Automony is enabling operators to access credit in a segment where options have historically been extremely limited. Their model unlocks income generation, supports entrepreneurship, and directly strengthens India's logistics backbone. By formalizing credit access for used commercial vehicle owners in Tier 2-3 India, the team is elevating livelihoods, improving mobility infrastructure, and unlocking economic growth.

We are proud to partner with Automony, a company building with purpose, precision, and unwavering execution. As India's logistics and mobility ecosystem continues to evolve, Automony is poised to become one of its most important enablers.

heading: Why We Invested in Ascend Capital
content:
# India's EV Revolution - An Inflection Point

In the years following COVID-19, India witnessed a dramatic shift in mobility trends. With rising fuel prices, growing awareness about climate impact, and strong government support, the country hit an inflection point in electric vehicle adoption especially in the electric three-wheeler (e3W) segment.

## A few numbers capture this momentum:

 - Electric three-wheelers today account for ~55-60% of total three-wheeler sales in India, making the segment the earliest and fastest to electrify.

 - Annual EV 3W sales have crossed 600,000 units, growing at a CAGR of over 30% in the last few years.

 - India is now the world's largest e-rickshaw market, with over 3 million vehicles on the road.

 The growth is undeniable but underneath this boom lies a reality often overlooked.

## The Credit Gap: India's Largest Missing Enabler 

Electric three-wheelers are primarily owned and operated by marginal income earners including daily-wage workers, small fleet operators, and individual driver-entrepreneurs. For them, access to reliable credit is not just an enabler but the difference between poverty and upward mobility. 

Yet the challenges are stark:

 - 40-50% of first-time buyers struggle to access formal loans.

 - Many rely on informal lenders who charge exorbitant interest rates of 30-50% annually, trapping families in cycles of debt.

 - Without structured financing, ownership remains unaffordable, despite strong economics: EV 3Ws have < INR 2/km operating cost, nearly 70% cheaper than ICE alternatives. 

This broken credit environment limits livelihoods, slows EV penetration, and leaves a massive economic opportunity untapped.

## A Cleaner, Greener Future: Why EVs Matter for Sustainability

 Beyond economics, the EV 3W revolution carries a powerful sustainability story. Electric three-wheelers reduce tailpipe emissions to zero, directly improving air quality in congested cities and small towns alike. An average EV 3W prevents 5-6 tonnes of CO₂ emissions per year compared to an ICE vehicle, a meaningful contribution in a country where urban air pollution is among the highest globally.

With cleaner grids, renewable energy adoption, and battery recycling innovations accelerating, EVs represent one of India's fastest pathways to climate-positive mobility. 

## Where We Saw the Opportunity

At Asha Ventures, our investment thesis in climate and financial inclusion has always been anchored in two principles: 

1. Transformational markets approaching an inflection point.

2. High-execution founders building foundational infrastructure in these markets. Ascend Capital sits at the intersection of both. 

By focusing on EV financing for underserved customers in Tier 2-4 India, Ascend is not just offering loans but it is unlocking income generation for thousands of households, many of whom are entering the formal credit ecosystem for the first time. 

## We were particularly energized by three strengths:

### 1. Deep underwriting capability for a new asset class 

Ascend has built credit models tailored for EV 3W borrowers, a segment where traditional banks still hesitate. Their data-led underwriting, field intelligence, and rigorous risk controls are among the strongest we have seen in early-stage financial institutions.

### 2. Distribution-first DNA 

With a presence across India's most active EV pockets, strong dealer networks, OEM partnerships, and high-touch servicing, Ascend understands the pulse of the market better than anyone. 

### 3. Exceptional execution by a mission-driven team

From our very first meeting, we were struck by the clarity, discipline, and ambition of the founding team. Their ability to scale rapidly while maintaining portfolio quality in a complex market is rare.

At Asha Ventures, we are proud to partner with a team that blends mission with execution and scale with empathy. The EV transformation has only just begun, and Ascend is poised to be one of the foundational pillars shaping its future enabling cleaner mobility, expanding livelihood opportunities, and accelerating India's transition to a sustainable economy.

heading: Rebuilding Healthcare Where It's Needed Most
content:
## Imagine this: 

A 52-year-old woman from Patna travelling over 1,400 kilometres to Hyderabad for a routine knee replacement surgery, a procedure easily accessible in most Tier 1 cities. For her family, it meant selling a small piece of land, taking weeks off work, and navigating uncertainty in an unfamiliar city. Sadly, this is not an isolated story. Every year, thousands of patients from Bihar undertake similar journeys to Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, or Hyderabad in search of what should be a basic right, reliable and affordable healthcare close to home. The emotional toll is exhausting, and the financial burden often crippling, leaving families trapped in a cycle of debt and despair.

## India's Healthcare Paradox

Since the pandemic, healthcare in India has gained unprecedented momentum. Public health spending has increased, private hospitals have expanded rapidly, and digital health innovations have bridged new gaps in access. Yet despite this progress, India's healthcare access and expenditure remain well below global standards. The country spends around 2.8% of GDP on healthcare, a fraction of the OECD average of 9%. For every world-class hospital in a metro, there are hundreds of districts where people still struggle for access to a basic doctor or clean hospital bed.

## Bihar: The Epicenter of Inequality

Home to nearly 127 million people, Bihar continues to rank among the lowest in most social and economic indicators. The state's per capita income stands at roughly INR 54,000 (2022-23), less than 30% of the national average, a glaring reminder of the unequal distribution of growth.

Despite its size, Bihar remains one of the most underserved states in terms of healthcare infrastructure and access. With over 88% of its population residing in rural areas, healthcare delivery is severely constrained by inadequate facilities and manpower. According to NITI Aayog, Bihar has just six hospital beds per one lakh population, compared to the national average of 24 beds, the lowest ratio in the country. The total hospital bed deficit, combining government and private sectors, exceeds 600,000 beds, leaving millions without timely or quality care.

## The Investment Gap in Bihar's Healthcare Infrastructure

Bihar has seen minimal private equity investment in healthcare infrastructure over the years. Most capital inflows into India's healthcare sector have been concentrated in metropolitan and Tier 1 cities, where established hospital chains, higher-paying patients, and predictable returns make investments less risky. In contrast, Bihar's underdeveloped ecosystem marked by limited private players and low insurance penetration has deterred institutional investors. As a result, the state continues to rely heavily on government facilities and individual practitioners, leaving a large gap in organized, quality healthcare capacity. 

# The Mediversal Vision

It was this reality that moved Navneet, Bhanu, and Jayant, the founders of Mediversal Hospitals. Having grown up in Bihar, they had witnessed firsthand how their communities suffered from poor access, overburdened public facilities, and unaffordable private care. After years of successful corporate careers, they chose to return home and build a healthcare system rooted in quality and equity. Their vision was simple but powerful to make world-class care accessible where it is needed the most.

## Bringing World-Class Care Home

Today, Mediversal operates two hospitals in Patna, a 100-bed multi-specialty facility and a 100-bed maternity and pediatric hospital supported by a primary care centre. The multi-specialty hospital offers a comprehensive range of clinical services including Orthopaedics, Cardiology, Internal Medicine, Neurosurgery, and Nephrology, along with specialized departments for Respiratory Medicine, Gastroenterology, General Surgery, and Neurology. Strategic partnerships with leading health-tech players have enabled IoT-based patient monitoring, AI-driven eICUs, and remote cardiac rehab solutions ensuring real-time interventions, improved outcomes, and enhanced safety.

The hospital also boasts Bihar's first neuro-navigation OT and BD ID/AST diagnostics facility, reinforcing its position as a regional technology leader. Backed by FDA/CE-approved equipment from global giants, the hospital delivers precise diagnostics and world-class interventions across specialties. This tech-led infrastructure not only elevates patient care but positions the hospital as a benchmark for scalable, high-impact healthcare in underserved markets.

Yet, Mediversal's greatest impact is not measured in equipment or technology. It lives in the lives it touches, in mothers who now have access to safe deliveries close to home, in families who no longer need to mortgage their gold to travel to Delhi for emergencies, and in young doctors who now choose to stay in Bihar because they can practice in institutions that match their training and values. Mediversal's hospitals have become anchors of trust in their communities.

## Our Belief

At Asha Ventures, we are proud to partner with Mediversal in this journey. When purpose meets vision, even the most neglected geographies can redefine what progress looks like. Mediversal is not just building hospitals but is rebuilding faith in the possibility of equitable healthcare for all.
